items.title: Lee Paige Interview, 1961-01-13
items.q: I think that I did quite a few Ethel Waters' numbers. I did one that she recorded and it's very popular and I did it quite frequently.

ctx.x: Lee, weren't you also influenced a lot by some of Ethel Waters' recordings? Wasn't there one of her numbers that you have done, you've added in your repertoire? Or a couple of them?

I think that I did quite a few Ethel Waters' numbers. I did one that she recorded and it's very popular and I did it quite frequently. And it's the blues tune, Stormy Weather, which is a very popular blues and it's a good coon shouting number. And on those type of numbers, I also do the original number of Pray For The Light To Go Out. I have the original music on it. I have the music there too. And it's quite popular. It also takes a long tug out and makes a preacher lay the Bible down. And all those type of…
Lee, when you first started in show business, didn't you work for a dollar and a half or a couple or two dollars or something like that? What were the wages?
